n1: The binding is underspecified: it contains “(...)” and asks only for the mug’s final position, while the criterion must distinguish completion from partial progress by comparing source and edited images. The traces repeatedly report the mug to the right, but the edited image visibly contains two mugs: one left of the headphones and one right. The right-hand mug may be an added/duplicated object, while the original mug appears displaced or blurred on the left; therefore the evidence does not establish that the requested mug was moved to the right. Make the node bind the mug across snapshots using its visual identity and assess its displacement relative to the headphones, explicitly accounting for duplicates/ambiguous correspondence. Preserve the criterion’s partial-progress distinction: movement toward the right without reaching the requested side is partial, not complete; unrelated added objects do not satisfy the edit. Do not force “partial” from the reference label alone—resolve the object correspondence from image evidence, and use unknown if it remains insufficient. The repeated high-confidence yes traces indicate a systematic binding/criterion failure, not a transport or dependency failure.

The edited image does place a mug to the right of the headphones, but it also shows another mug left of them and a conspicuous blurred blue mug-shaped remnant at the source location. Thus the repeated “complete/yes” judgments appear to assess only whether a right-side mug exists, not whether the requested mug was moved and the edit is complete; this conflicts with the partial reference and the rubric’s all-changes-complete criterion. Repair the node’s binding/criteria to track the source mug across source and edited images, distinguish relocation from duplication or residual artifacts, and represent partial progress when the target appears at the destination but remains at or is duplicated from its original location. Keep insufficient visual evidence unresolved rather than inferring completion. The traces are consistently high-confidence and valid, with no dependency or transport failures, so focus on the visual criterion and object correspondence—not confidence or routing.
